# 2 Chronicles Chapter 30 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Hezekiah sent word to all Israel and Judah and also wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh, inviting them to come to the LORD's temple in Jerusalem to celebrate the Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel.

**2** The king, his officials, and the whole assembly in Jerusalem decided to celebrate the Passover in the second month,

**3** since they hadn't been able to celebrate it at the regular time — not enough priests had consecrated themselves, and the people hadn't assembled in Jerusalem.

**4** The plan seemed right to the king and the whole assembly.

**5** They decided to send a proclamation throughout all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, calling the people to come to Jerusalem and celebrate the Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel. It hadn't been widely celebrated as prescribed.

**6** Couriers went throughout Israel and Judah carrying letters from the king and his officials, which read: "People of Israel, return to the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, so that He may return to those of you who have escaped the hand of the kings of Assyria.

**7** Don't be like your fathers and brothers, who were unfaithful to the LORD, the God of their ancestors. He made them an object of horror, as you can see.

**8** Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. Submit to the LORD. Come to His sanctuary, which He has consecrated forever. Serve the LORD your God, so that His fierce anger will turn away from you.

**9** If you return to the LORD, then your relatives and children will be shown compassion by their captors and will return to this land. For the LORD your God is gracious and compassionate. He will not turn His face from you if you return to Him."

**10** The couriers traveled from town to town through Ephraim and Manasseh, as far as Zebulun, but people ridiculed and mocked them.

**11** Nevertheless, some from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.

**12** God's hand was on Judah too, giving them unity of heart to carry out what the king and his officials had ordered in accordance with the word of the LORD.

**13** A very large crowd gathered in Jerusalem to celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread in the second month.

**14** They removed the pagan altars in Jerusalem and cleared out the incense altars, throwing them into the Kidron Valley.

**15** They slaughtered the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the second month. The priests and Levites were ashamed and consecrated themselves and brought burnt offerings to the LORD's temple.

**16** They took their regular positions as prescribed in the Law of Moses the man of God. The priests splashed the blood handed to them by the Levites.

**17** Since many in the assembly had not consecrated themselves, the Levites had to kill the Passover lambs for all who were ceremonially unclean and couldn't consecrate their lambs to the LORD.

**18** Although many people — especially from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun — had not purified themselves, they ate the Passover anyway, contrary to what was prescribed. But Hezekiah prayed for them: "May the LORD, who is good, pardon everyone

**19** who sets their heart on seeking God — the LORD, the God of their ancestors — even if they're not clean according to the rules of the sanctuary."

**20** And the LORD heard Hezekiah and healed the people.

**21** The Israelites who were in Jerusalem celebrated the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days with great joy, while the Levites and priests praised the LORD every day, accompanied by loud instruments.

**22** Hezekiah spoke encouragingly to all the Levites who showed excellent skill in serving the LORD. For the seven days they ate their portion of the festival offerings, sacrificing fellowship offerings and giving thanks to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.

**23** The whole assembly then agreed to celebrate for seven more days. So they celebrated with joy for another seven days.

**24** Hezekiah king of Judah provided 1,000 bulls and 7,000 sheep and goats for the assembly, and the officials provided 1,000 bulls and 10,000 sheep and goats. A large number of priests consecrated themselves.

**25** The entire assembly of Judah, the priests and Levites, all who had come from Israel, the foreigners from Israel, and those living in Judah — all celebrated joyfully.

**26** There was great joy in Jerusalem, because nothing like this had happened there since the days of Solomon son of David, king of Israel.

**27** The Levitical priests stood and blessed the people. God heard them, and their prayer reached heaven, His holy dwelling place.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **30:9**: "The LORD your God is gracious and compassionate. He will not turn His face from you if you return to Him" — this is the gospel of the Old Testament, written on royal stationery and hand-delivered by couriers to every city in Israel.

- **30:10-11**: Most people laughed. A few came. The Chronicler doesn't sugarcoat it: revival is not universally popular. But it only takes a remnant.

- **30:18-20**: Hezekiah prays: "God, they didn't purify themselves properly, but their hearts are in the right place." God heals them. This is one of the most radical moments in the Old Testament — God values heart-direction over ritual precision.

- **30:26**: "Nothing like this since Solomon." The Chronicler is saying: this is what happens when you reopen the temple, reinstate the worship, and invite everyone — including your enemies — to come back to God.


— PNEUMA
